entries.title: Autocomplete and Ctrl+K rank all matching blocks globally before capping, so a strong match is never omitted by graph traversal order
entries.notes: GH #186. Page/tag candidates were already a global BinaryHeap top-k, but block-ref production walked pages in traversal order and broke at the cap with a flat score, so a strong block match on a late page was silently omitted. Fixed: query_plan::execute_blocks builds a global bounded-heap top-k with real per-block relevance (match-class > word-boundary > earlier-offset > shorter-text > fewer-occurrences, deterministic tie-break by (page rel_path, in-page index) — bare traversal index was nondeterministic because walk_page_files reads fs::read_dir unsorted; regression block_search_topk_ties_sort_rel_path_with_reversed_page_snapshot forces a reversed page snapshot); OG caps adopted (inline pages 100 / block-refs 20; Ctrl+K 100/100 ranked pool, existing chunked presentation); autocomplete fold NFKC->NFC to match #137/backend. Fail-before proven (best block on last page survives + ranks ahead of weaker earlier matches; NFC-vs-NFKC ordering). Manager-reviewed block top-k + green (tine-core 455, autocomplete 50, component 20); not separately adversarially verified (search-ordering, lower risk than #137).

entries.title: Settings panel scrolls on narrow/mobile viewports so every setting is reachable

entries.title: Accepting a page/block-ref completion while editing inside an existing ref rewrites the whole ref, leaving no stray closing bracket (Logseq parity)
entries.notes: GH #199. Editing inside an already-closed [[word]] (e.g. autopaired [[second]], arrow-left, type 'first ' -> [[first |second]]) and accepting a completion left a stray ]] ([[first]]second]]) because Block.tsx replaceTrigger only swallowed the closing pair when it sat IMMEDIATELY at the caret (ref.value.slice(t.end,t.end+2)===pair). OG-verified (og@6e7afa8, findings in tine-agents specs notes): OG's query range is [[->caret (matches Tine's detectTrigger, unchanged), but on accept OG scans forward from the caret to the ref's closer (:end-pattern ]]), strips it (postfix-fn) and rewrites the whole region. Fix: new pure refCompletionEnd(value,end,insertedText) in autocomplete.ts scans forward on the CURRENT LINE for the closer matching the completion's suffix (]]/))/}}), returning just past it or the caret when none ahead; replaceTrigger now uses it. Covers page AND block refs (same latent defect) and the latent end-caret ]]]] doubling. Not a regression: latent since the autocomplete feature shipped (e54ad36e, 2026-06-14). Fail-before proven (pre-fix immediate-only range yields [[first]]second]]); 7 unit cases (mid/end/unclosed/block/line-bounded/non-ref/reporter-integration); Block.referenceAuthoring + tagAutocomplete + selectionWrap render tests still green (wiring regression guard). Delegated to gpt-5.6-terra (xhigh), manager-reviewed + gates run. Real-app editor confirmation pending on next deploy (pure-logic fix, proportionate).

entries.notes: OG-parity catalogue pick (og-parity.assets-pdf-media.raw-remote-image-url, LIVE-BACKLOG s9). Extension set = Tine's canonical mediaKind (media.ts) rather than OG's literal list (Tine adds avif/m4v/oga/opus; lacks ico) -- an intentional harmless presentation-heuristic difference, noted per AGENTS parity doctrine. entries.notes: Blocking core operation. GH #623 comment 17 (Windows): trashing an attachment failed with 'asset is referenced; refresh the orphan inventory'. Cause: onTrashAsset removed the token with setRaw (debounced save) and called trashAsset at once; og's backend orphan check (absent on master) reads the published graph, which still held the reference. Fix: flushPage(block page) first, then trashAsset; a save failure trashes nothing. The backend returns the typed outcome 'trashed' | 'referenced' (no error-text matching); 'referenced' keeps the file, the block edit stands, and the user is told the file is still used elsewhere. Settings orphan trash reports the same outcome. PDF area-image retirement and page delete use generic (non-orphan) trash and are not on this path. Fail-before: the new render test run against the unfixed inline.tsx fails 3 of 3 (trash fired before any save; no unsaved-edit refusal). Native Windows unverified; Linux native run recorded in RECEIPT-OG-E623.md.

entries.title: Open in new window opens a page in its own desktop window with its own panes, tabs and history; edits there save like main, no close loses typed text, and open windows come back at the next launch

entries.notes: OG-MULTIWINDOW (og feature, desktop only; context menu, page title menu and palette entry points). Blocking core operation plus exact safety: every close door (pane close, title bar, native destroy without a close request, main quit, main reload, graph switch, session restore) disposes once, ends an edit in the window and flushes saves. Fail-before for the title-bar close: the native journey lost the last typed letter ('closed at onc') because Tauri relayed the close request before WebKit delivered the queued keystroke; disposal now waits for input to settle (at most 1 s). The render test 'a title-bar close lets input already on its way land' fails against the pre-fix module. Linux native run plus 5-run burn-in. Hosted ci.yml scope multiwindow (scripts/hosted-multiwindow.mjs, OS input, exact page-file assertions) run 37495725604 on e39f57d2f passed on Linux, Windows and macOS: open from the palette, type and save, keep typing with main minimized (saved 0.7 s / 3.1 s / 1.3 s after 5.5 minutes minimized), and a title-bar close right after typing keeps the text. Review fixes (manager review of og-mw): a native destroy always unregisters the window (Rust workspace-window-destroyed event), close/open polls run on the popup clock as well as main's, main's own pagehide flushes, interface zoom reaches each window's webview, a graph switch closes windows only after its access prompt and PDF drain, and the query export dialog stays in its window. No right sidebar, left sidebar, file drop or in-window IME guarantees.

entries.title: The system tray is optional and never leaves an invisible app: tray icon with Open Tine, Quick Capture and Quit, minimize to tray, and start minimized to tray, with a shown window whenever no tray exists

coverage.scenario: with a fake StatusNotifier host: the app registers a tray item whose menu offers Open Tine, Quick Capture and Quit, starts with main hidden while its graph loads, Open Tine shows main and an edit there reaches disk, minimizing hides main from the window list, a second launch shows it, the tray host leaving shows a hidden main and turns minimize-to-tray off, a late-appearing host gets the icon while main stays hidden, tray Quit with a hidden graph-less main and a graph window holding an unsaved edit leaves that edit on disk, and close still quits; with no tray host the same settings show the window and Settings is told why

entries.notes: GH #625, og-tray. Stateful UX plus an invisible-app safety rule. Fail-before: with behaviour() changed so start_hidden ignores whether the icon exists, the unit tests a_tray_that_could_not_be_created_shows_the_window and only_a_bare_or_capture_launch_starts_hidden fail, and the native journey's no-tray-host scenario fails with 'the window stayed hidden: the user would be left with an invisible app'. Linux native run drives the real AppIndicator and its dbusmenu menu through a fake StatusNotifierWatcher; AppIndicator delivers no left click on Linux, so the click rule (show, or hide when visible and focused) is covered by the decision-function unit test only. Review round (2026-10-06): host loss at runtime (NameOwnerChanged watch), a second launch reveals main only when the tray hid it, autostart waits up to 8 s for a late host, no activation-policy/Dock change on macOS, and the quit race is closed at the root (exit waits for every closing window; state::may_exit + ClosingWindows). Fail-before by mutation: without the watch the host-left step fails; with the old graph-count exit rule scenario 3 loses the unsaved edit; with the wait disabled scenario 4 fails. Windows and macOS: hosted compilation (ci.yml windows and multiwindow scopes); no native tray journey was run there.

entries.title: A user can discover and recover customizing Tine's look: documented --tine-* tokens reach the rendering, logseq/custom.css edited outside Tine is re-applied live without reopening, Edit custom.css creates the file if missing, and Disable custom CSS is a session-only safe mode

coverage.scenario: a graph whose custom.css sets --tine-bullet-color shows that bullet color at open; an editor-style temp+rename save, an in-place rewrite, a delete and a re-create of the file each change the rendered bullet within seconds with the window never reloading; the same token, set from custom.css, also drives the embed background, bullet size, tag color, content width, page title size, base font size and content font in the browser harness (scripts/shot-theme-tokens.mjs tokens)

entries.notes: GH #610, og-theming. Stateful UX. Fail-before: with the store's custom.css lane disabled, the native journey fails at the first outside save ('bullet is rgb(1, 2, 3), wanted rgb(10, 120, 30)'), the store unit test external_custom_css_edits_publish_and_own_writes_do_not_echo and src-tauri watcher::an_external_custom_css_edit_is_announced_and_an_own_write_is_not fail; with a documented token removed from theme.css or an undocumented --tine-* name added, src/themeTokens.guard.test.ts fails with the rule and an exemplar. Defaults reproduce today's rendering: scripts/shot-theme-tokens.mjs capture on the pre-change and post-change builds gives byte-identical light and dark screenshots and equal computed styles. Edit custom.css hands the file to the system opener, which a native run must not start; its create-if-missing, oversized-file and directory behaviour is covered in crates/tine-graph-features/tests/custom_css_edit.rs. Android has no editor hand-off (a file-path hint is shown), live reload and Disable custom CSS apply wherever the watcher runs. The inspector is part of release builds (tauri devtools feature): on the Linux release binary under xvfb a Web Inspector window opened and closed from Ctrl+Shift+J and opened from Settings > Developer tools (evidence in tine-agents/evidence/og-theming); Windows and macOS rely on the same feature and are not proven here. Tine does not add a right-click Inspect Element. A transient live re-read failure keeps the last stylesheet and retries once (src/customCss.test.tsx), a later read supersedes an earlier one, an unchanged file is not re-hashed under poll mode (store test), and a public token set with html{} or :root{} in custom.css overrides the default (scripts/shot-theme-tokens.mjs overrides; src/themeTokens.guard.test.ts :where declaration rule).
